failure_summary.description: The agent chose an option that silently shrank the parameter range to an invented subset ((-1,2]∪{∞}), although the stem asked for a statement over the full range (-1,∞]. An option with the same conclusion on the stem's full range was available and strictly stronger.
The agent did not ask where the unexplained cutoff p=2 came from. The stem has no such threshold, and no derivation was given to justify cutting the range.

patch.reasoning: The skill already says to respect the stem's range, but only warns against extending it past the stem. It does not warn against options that shrink the range to a subset while keeping the same conclusion. That subset option is a truncation of the full-range option, so the full-range option implies it. This edit makes the rule two-sided and adds a short, visible check near the top of the workflow. The check compares each option's range with the stem's range, flags thresholds that appear only in options, and says the full-range option wins unless a concrete counterexample is produced. It is written in terms of option structure only, so it does not depend on this topic.

edits.target: The option that states the conclusion for the stem's own β without altering the range is usually the faithful one.
edits.content: The option that states the conclusion for the stem's own β without altering the range is usually the faithful one. The rule is two-sided: an option that silently SHRINKS the stem's range (e.g. p in (-1,2]∪{∞} when the stem says every p in (-1,∞]) is a truncation of the full-range option whenever the conclusion is identical. If the full-range option is not refuted, it implies the shrunken one and wins.

edits.target: 7. Commit once exactly one option survives (not false, not strictly weaker than another survivor, no unjustified extra clause). Do not switch to an option that merely looks more general or elaborate unless its extra content is justified.
edits.content: 7b. Range-echo check (write it out): list each option's parameter and object range next to the stem's range. (i) An option whose range equals the stem's and whose conclusion is the plain one is the default hub. (ii) A threshold or cutoff that appears only in the options (such as 'p ≤ 2', 'N ≥ 3', 'finite p > 2') and not in the stem is an invented restriction. Keep it only if you can name a concrete counterexample just beyond the cutoff. Without one, prefer the option that covers the stem's full range. (iii) An option that adds 'but for some … outside the range it fails' needs a witness you can actually produce. Do not pick a restricted-range option out of caution.
